nina: Quick heads-up — onboarding polaris-32k (int8) and I'm seeing a reproducible drift after ~18k tokens compared to fp16. Short repro attached.

oscar: Can you paste the minimal repro command?

nina: Sure — run this on the new images (polaris-int8 build):
```
python repro.py --model polaris-32k --quant int8 --prompt-file tests/long_20k.txt --seed 42 --out /tmp/pol_out.json
```
Outputs: fp16 vs int8 divergence: first mismatch at token 18234, sample perplexities: fp16=12.3, int8=17.9 (rough numbers from quick run).

sasha: That's pretty big. Does it look like token substitution/shift or growing drift?

nina: More like token substitution with cascading divergence (prefix matches until ~18k then majority mismatch). Probable context/caching issue rather than greedy decode bug.

lee: Quick hypothesis: rotary embedding scaling mismatch after quantization of sin/cos tables or a phase scaling truncation. We saw similar amplitude slips on other int8 bringups. Can you run with ROPE debug logs?

nina: Trying now. Using env var:
```
ROPE_DEBUG=1 ROPE_VERBOSE=2 python repro.py --model polaris-32k --quant int8 --prompt-file tests/long_20k.txt
```
Log snippet: 
```
[ropecache] token_idx=18230 phase=0.87234 sin=0.99982 cos=0.01856 quant_round_err=1.2e-3
[ropecache] token_idx=18231 phase=0.87256 sin=0.99981 cos=0.01873 quant_round_err=2.1e-3
[ropecache] mismatch_detected token_idx=18234 kv_key_hash=0x3f12ab
```

oscar: If kv_key_hash differs between fp16 and int8, it points to preprocessing table rounding not the serving KV transport. Can you dump the sin/cos tables used by kernels?

lee: I'll add a small kernel dump that prints the first N sin/cos pairs and their quantized encodings. Patch incoming: https://github.com/redwood-inference/polaris/compare/rotary-dump-int8 (WIP).

sasha: Meanwhile I'll run the long-context eval set (long-bench-20k) across latest fp16, int8 and int4 experimental. We need metric diffs (perp, ROUGE on generated completions, and token drift histogram). Will post results here.

ci-bot: Build #7824 for polaris-int8 completed on image polaris-int8:v20260323 — artifacts at s3://redwood-ci/polaris/7824/.

nina: Thanks. Quick note: reproducer also shows a slight increase in latency after 15k tokens on int8 (maybe cache fallback causing extra memcpy).

oscar: I'll check runtime side — look for unexpected KV cache evictions or fallback to cpu path. Running tracing now against the same workload.

lee: If this is quant rounding of sin/cos, quick mitigation is to store sin/cos in fp16 and convert to fp32 inside the kernel rather than using int8 table lookup. That avoids phase drift for very long sequences. But cost/latency tradeoff needs evaluation.

sasha: Eval results (first run): fp16 perp=12.27, int8 perp=18.0, int4 perp=33.4. Token divergence histogram shows spike at >18k for int8 and earlier for int4. Putting full CSV in GDrive: https://drive.redwood/polaris/long-bench-20k/2026-03-23/results.csv

nina: Good. Action items:
- nina will open issue with repro + logs (ISSUE-4821)
- lee to bisect quant kernel range and dump sin/cos encodings (lee assigned)
- oscar to run runtime KV trace and confirm whether kv_key_hash mismatch originates in precompute vs transport
- sasha to run expanded eval (10 seeds) and attach metric diffs

oscar: If runtime shows identical keys but different values coming back, we need to look at serialization/quantized memcpy paths. I'll check pinned commits that touched kv-serialize in the last month.

lee: Quick dev note: trying a change to compute rotary using an fp16 table promoted to fp32 in the kernel. Benchmark locally shows +2% token latency but removes the phase drift in a small smoke test up to 25k tokens. Pushing PR after tests.

nina: Great. Marking triage: high priority for onboarding (dedicated customers expect 32k context). Please tag me on PRs. :eyes:

sasha: Will also add a regression alert to Optimize so future int8 onboards trigger a longctx smoke harness.

ci-bot: ISSUE-4821 created by nina — https://issues.redwood/4821 (polaris-32k int8 longctx token divergence).

nina: Thanks team — we'll reconvene after lee/oscar have initial bisect/traces. If either of you finds quick mitigation, we can roll a patched image to canary.

oscar: Sounds good. I'll report back by EOD with trace summary.

lee: I'll post bisect results and kernel dump link within a few hours.

sasha: I'll queue the 10-seed eval and share charts.

nina: Closing for now — keeping this thread as the source of truth for the triage.
